dedup.note: input.json delivers pfs-2 twice (identical payload, same provider_ref). unique(account_id, provider_ref) + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (§4.1 step 4) means only ONE fills row for pfs-2 is ever written. The fills list below has exactly 4 rows, not 5.

invariant_checks.invariant: grouping is deterministic for identical input, regardless of feed arrival order (00-foundation §9.2; Module 02 §4.2 'ordered by filled_at, id')
invariant_checks.note: input.json's fills array arrives in feed order [pfs-2(dup), pfs-2(dup), pfs-3, pfs-1, pfs-exit] — none of it filled_at order. Block/grouping derivation must re-sort by (filled_at, id) before running the running-volume algorithm; the result above does not depend on array order.

invariant_checks.invariant: sum of fill P&L equals trade P&L (00-foundation §9.2)

scoping_note: This fixture does not cover the true exact-timestamp-tie (filled_at, id) tiebreak — the three entry fills are 0.35s and 0.55s apart, which is realistic sub-second broker granularity but not a literal tie. A genuine (filled_at, id)-tiebreak test would need to pin insertion order as a second, separate concern and is left out of Phase 0's required set.
